text:
Sean Gallagher: Hey folks — for the data residency enforcement rollout, can we get a concrete list of metrics/events we’re emitting so we can start alerting? Specifically looking for: (1) violations/denies at gateway, (2) policy evaluator failures, (3) any routing fallback counters, and (4) downstream write blocks. Also need guidance on thresholds so we don’t page ourselves into oblivion during canary/beta.

Sergio Costa: +1. I saw a stub dashboard PR mentioned in standup but not sure what’s final. What’s the Prometheus metric names + labels? Need to know cardinality too (org_id labels = risky).

Amara Diallo: Gateway side: we’ve got middleware tagging the request context. Proposed metrics (names in PR but can align to standards):
- `residency_check_total{decision="allow|deny", reason="region_mismatch|policy_missing|evaluator_unavailable|fallback_blocked", product="hosted|dedicated", region="us-east|eu-west", tier="enterprise|pro"}`
- `residency_check_latency_ms_bucket{...}`
Also structured error response uses `error.code=RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH` etc. We can emit a counter by error code too but might be redundant.

Allison Grant: Please don’t put `org_id` in metric labels. If you need per-tenant debugging, rely on logs/traces + audit events, or sample-based exemplars. We can include `org_tier`, `region`, `policy_mode` (pinned vs allowed list), and maybe `deployment`.

Rafael Mendes: For alerts, I’d prefer burn-rate style on SLO-impacting stuff. Violations might be “expected” if customers misconfigure SDKs. So: alert on sudden spikes (delta) rather than absolute rates.

Sean Gallagher: Exactly. I’m thinking two categories:
1) Platform health: evaluator down, middleware failing open/closed incorrectly, cross-region routing attempts.
2) Customer misconfig signals: increased denies but shouldn’t page on that unless it’s widespread or correlated with a release.

Logan Wright: Telemetry side we’ll also tag traces with `residency.decision`, `residency.reason`, `residency.requested_region`, `residency.effective_region`. For metrics, we have a pipeline counter for audit events too but that’s more for evidence than paging.

Nadia Rahman: Audit events planned:
- `residency.policy_evaluated` (allow) and `residency.violation` (deny)
Fields include org/project/workspace ids (in the event payload), requested region, resolved region, policy version hash, decision reason. SIEM export will include these. Not great for alerting but good for per-customer investigation.

Sergio Costa: Ok, alert candidates I’m drafting:
- `policy_evaluator_request_errors_rate` > X% for 5m (page)
- `residency_check_total{decision="deny"}` spike above baseline (ticket?)
- `routing_cross_region_attempt_total` > 0 when `policy_mode="pinned"` (page?)
Do we have a routing counter?

Mina Haddad: Router will emit:
- `routing_fallback_blocked_total{reason="pinned_region", from_region, to_region, product}`
- `routing_cross_region_fallback_total{allowed="true|false", policy_mode, from_region, to_region}`
But note: when pinned, cross-region fallback should be blocked at decision time; “attempt” is basically “we would’ve fallen back but policy prevented it.” That’s useful as early warning for capacity issues in a region.

Marcus Lin: From Security POV: we want high confidence that “fail closed” is actually happening. I’d like an alert if we ever see `residency_check_total{reason="evaluator_unavailable", decision="allow"}` (i.e., fail-open), because that’s a policy violation scenario.

Amara Diallo: Agree. Current design is fail-closed for pinned policies, but there’s a feature flag path for early beta where we can temporarily return `503` vs a deny (still no model execution). We should make the metric explicit with `enforcement_mode="strict|beta"`.

Allison Grant: +1 add `enforcement_mode` label, but keep values low-cardinality. Also please don’t include raw `requested_region` if that can be arbitrary; map it to a known set (or “unknown”).

Sean Gallagher: On thresholds: what’s the expected baseline deny rate during canary?

Nadia Rahman: For canary cohort we expect some initial churn because SDK region defaults won’t match for a subset of customers. Docs will lag a bit. So deny rates could be non-trivial (like 0.5–2% of requests) for the cohort.

Rafael Mendes: That’s exactly why paging on deny rate is a trap. Suggest:
- Page only on *platform inability to evaluate policy* or *unexpected allow in strict mode*.
- For deny spikes: create a warning alert routed to #eng-platform / #support-readiness after N minutes, not pager.

Sergio Costa: Proposed alerting (v1):
P0 Page:
- Policy evaluator 5xx rate > 2% for 5m OR p95 latency > 250ms for 10m (affects admission)
- `residency_fail_open_total` > 0 (in strict mode)
- `audit_exporter_drop_rate` > threshold (if we treat audit as compliance-critical)
P1 Ticket/Slack:
- Deny rate > 5% for 10m across any region+tier (not per org)
- `routing_fallback_blocked_total` increasing fast (capacity signal)
We can tune after baseline.

GrafanaBot: Panel created: "Residency enforcement / Decision rate" (draft) — datasource: prometheus-prod — query: sum(rate(residency_check_total[5m])) by (decision, reason, region). (requested by @sergio)

Sean Gallagher: Love it. Can we add gating so we don’t alert while feature flag is ramping?

Sergio Costa: Yep. If we label metrics with `rollout_phase="off|canary|beta|ga"` (or just derive via cohort?), we can silence alerts in canary. But deriving in PromQL is messy. Better: alert rules check a config flag metric (like `feature_flag_residency_enforcement_enabled{env, region} 0/1`). Do we have that?

Amara Diallo: We can emit a cheap gauge from gateway config reload: `residency_enforcement_enabled{env, region} 0/1` and `residency_enforcement_mode{env, region, mode}` as 0/1 series. That should help for alert conditions.

Allison Grant: Please don’t do `residency_enforcement_mode` with mode as a label and value 0/1 per mode unless you must. Prefer `residency_enforcement_config{mode="strict"}` as a label with value 1, but only one series per env/region.

Rafael Mendes: Also: for the deny-rate warning, use “newly enabled” suppression. I’ve seen rollouts where first hour is noisy but then stabilizes. We can set the alert to require 30m sustained, or add an inhibition rule for 2h after enable.

Sean Gallagher: OK action items:
- @Amara confirm final metric names/labels for gateway checks + add the enable gauge.
- @Mina confirm routing counters + whether blocked fallback should be a warning signal for capacity.
- @Sergio draft alert rules w/ paging only on evaluator health + fail-open in strict.
- I’ll coordinate with Support so they know deny spikes might happen during beta and where to look.

Sergio Costa: Sounds good. I’ll wire alerts to: PagerDuty for evaluator health + fail-open; everything else to #eng-sre + #eng-platform with runbook link.

Marcus Lin: Please include in the runbook: how to prove no cross-region processing occurred (audit event queries) when a customer asks.

Sean Gallagher: Yep — will link the residency violation runbook + audit event spec once it’s merged.

Rafael Mendes: Final note: remember cardinality in `reason`. Keep the set small and stable. Don’t encode exception ids etc.

Amara Diallo: Ack. Reasons will be an enum (6-8 values max). No freeform strings.

Sean Gallagher: Great. Thanks all.
